input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: _interpret_color no longer checks the 0..255 range, rejects bools or validates tuple length, and an unknown name raises KeyError instead of ValueError
- failure path: style('x', fg=300) emits an escape with an out-of-range index instead of raising ValueError; fg=True is now accepted where it used to raise, formatting as palette index 1; an unknown color name surfaces as TypeError from the caller's except clause instead of a ValueError naming the color

Reviewer finding
- description: Removing color component validation allows invalid palette indices and RGB components to produce invalid ANSI sequences.
- rationale: For example, style('text', fg=256) or style('text', fg=(256, 0, 0)) previously raised ValueError. These inputs now generate escape sequences with out-of-range color values, silently passing malformed styling to the terminal instead of rejecting the invalid color.
critique: The finding identifies the removed 0..255 range validation in color interpretation. It describes the same outcome: out-of-range palette indices or RGB components now produce escape sequences instead of raising ValueError. It does not mention bools or unknown names, but the range-check part of the labeled defect is matched through the same mechanism.
